==English==
{{wp|,+ (missile)}}
[[File:Dart.svg|thumb|280px|right|Parts: 1.[[tip|Tip]] 2.[[barrel|Barrel]] 3.[[O-ring]] 4.[[shaft|Shaft]] 5.[[collar|Collar]] 6.[[flight|Flight]] 7.[[protector|Protector]].]]

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/dɑːt/|a=RP}}
* {{enPR|därt|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/dɑɹt/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-dart.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|[daɹt̚]|[daɹɾ̥]|a=Ottawa Valley}}
* {{audio|en|EN-AU ck1 dart.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɑː(ɹ)t|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:dart|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|dart}}, from {{der|en|fro|dart}}, {{m|fro|dard|t=dart}}, from {{der|en|la-med|dardus}}, from {{der|en|frk|*darōþu|t=dart, spear}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*darōþuz|t=dart, spear}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰerh₃-|t=to leap, spring}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|wifer}}.

Compare {{cog|goh|tart|t=javelin, dart}}, {{cog|ang|daroþ}}, {{m|ang|dearod|t=javelin, spear, dart}}, {{cog|sv|dart|t=dart, dagger}}, {{cog|is|darraður}}, {{m|is|darr}}, {{m|is|dör|t=dart, spear}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A pointed missile weapon, intended to be thrown by the hand; for example, a short lance or [[javelin]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1769|author=Oxford Standard Text|chapter=[[s:Bible (King James)|King James Bible]]|title=[[s:Bible (King James)/2 Samuel|2 Samuel]]|section=xviii, 14
|passage=Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three '''darts''' in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.}}
# Any sharp-pointed missile weapon, such as an arrow.
# {{lb|en|sometimes|figurative}} Anything resembling such a missile; something that pierces or wounds like such a weapon.
# A small object with a [[pointed]] tip at one end and [[feather]]s at the other,  which is [[throw]]n at a [[target]] in the game of [[darts]].
# {{lb|en|geometry}} A [[concave]] [[quadrilateral]] similar in shape to a [[chevron]] or [[arrowhead]].
# {{lb|en|Australia|New Zealand|Canada|colloquial}} A cigarette.
# {{lb|en|military}} A dart-shaped target towed behind an aircraft to train shooters.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1988|journal=Michigan Aviation|volume=21-25|page=62
|passage=Fighter aircraft also use restricted areas for target shooting at '''darts''' towed 1500 feet behind another aircraft.}}
# {{lb|en|Australia|obsolete}} A [[plan]] or [[scheme]].
# A sudden or fast movement.
#: {{ux|en|[[soon as|Soon as]] I felt the floor tremor I made a '''dart''' for the door.}}
# {{lb|en|sewing}} A fold that is stitched on a garment.
#* {{RQ:Economist|year=2013| url=http://www.economist.com/news/obituary/21581962-nadezhda-nadia-popova-night-bomber-pilot-died-july-8th-aged-91-nadia-popova| title=Nadia Popova| passage=Somehow she managed, with a cinched waist here and a few '''darts''' there, to look like a Hollywood star.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107113632/https://www.economist.com/news/obituary/21581962-nadezhda-nadia-popova-night-bomber-pilot-died-july-8th-aged-91-nadia-popova|archivedate=7 November 2017}}
# A [[dace]] (fish) ({{taxfmt|Leuciscus leuciscus|species}}).
# Any of various species of [[hesperiid]] [[butterfly]].

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|darten}}, from the noun (see above).

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To throw with a sudden effort or thrust; to [[hurl]] or [[launch]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To send forth suddenly or rapidly; to [[emit]]; to shoot.
#: {{ux|en|As the sun '''darted''' forth his beams, she '''darted''' a meaningful glance at me.}}
#* {{RQ:Pope Pastorals|year=1717|title=Autumn|page=28|passage=''[[w:Pan (god)|Pan]]'' came, and ask'd, what magic caus'd my ſmart, / Or what ill eyes malignant glances '''dart'''?}}
#* {{RQ:Heller Catch-22|The Eternal City|432|Yossarian responded to the thought by slipping away stealthily from the police and almost tripped over the feet of a burly woman of forty hastening across the intersection guiltily, '''darting''' furtive, vindictive glances behind her toward a woman of eighty with thick, bandaged ankles doddering after her in a losing pursuit.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To shoot with a dart, especially a [[tranquilizer dart]].
#: {{usex|en|They had to '''dart''' the animal to get close enough to help}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To fly or pass swiftly, like a dart; to move rapidly in one direction; to shoot out quickly.
#: {{ux|en|The flying man '''darted''' eastward.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To start and run with speed; to shoot rapidly along.
#: {{syn|en|dash|steam}}
#: {{ux|en|The deer '''darted''' from the thicket.}}
#: {{ux|en|The fish '''darted''' under a stone.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Daniel Taylor|title=Luis Suárez strikes twice as Barcelona teach Manchester City a lesson|date=24 February 2015|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/feb/24/manchester-city-barcelona-champions-league-match-report
|passage=By half-time, it was almost a surprise that the away side had restricted themselves to only one more goal. Messi, again, was prominently involved, '''darting''' past Fernando and then Zabaleta.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013064843/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/feb/24/manchester-city-barcelona-champions-league-match-report|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
#* {{quote-journal
|en
|date=December 29, 2010
|author=Mark Vesty
|title=Wigan 2 - 2 Arsenal
|work=BBC
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9322845.stm
|page=
|passage=The impressive Frenchman drove forward with purpose down the right before cutting infield and '''darting''' in between Vassiriki Diaby and Koscielny.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017180102/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9322845.stm|archivedate=17 October 2022}}
